history.period: Claimed antiquity of thousands of years; Katyuri-era attribution unverified
history.summary: Kapileshwar Mahadev is a Shiva cave temple on a steep hill at Ancholi village, about 3 km from Pithoragarh, near Takaura and Takari villages, at the confluence of the Shakuni and Fadka rivers. Sources attribute its construction to the Katyuri dynasty and claim an age of thousands of years. Legend says Sage Kapil (held locally to be an incarnation of Vishnu) meditated in this cave, giving the temple its name; inside are a Swayambhu (self-manifested) Shiva Linga and natural rock formations of Shiva, Surya and Shivalinga. A second legend tells of two snakes that competed to destroy each other's temples (Kapileshwar's vs Mauna's), with white markings on the riverbank stones said to be their traces. Reaching the shrine means climbing 200+ steps, with an old Bhagavati temple midway; the cave passage is narrow (~10 m deep, described as ~25 ft) and the temple commands views of the Soar Valley and Himalayan peaks. Worship rights rest with Nath-tradition Goswami families. One source (sacredyatra) says the Archaeological Department has taken the temple under protection and a museum was being built (verify). Coordinates are for the Kapileshwar Mandir peak (OSM/Wikidata via Mapcarta), immediately adjacent to the temple - verify exact temple point.

name: Kapileshwar Mahadev Temple
town_description: Pithoragarh is a Himalayan town in the Kumaon region of Uttarakhand and headquarters of Pithoragarh district, set in the Soar (Sor) Valley at about 1,650 m. A former Chand-dynasty and later Gorkha stronghold, it is the gateway to the Kailash-Mansarovar route and the Johar and Darma valleys, and is served by the nearby Naini Saini airport.
tradition: Shaivism; worship rights with Nath-tradition Goswami families
